objective: Make the monitoring debounce policy an explicit, validated server configuration instead of an implicit AlertPolicy() constructed inside HealthStore: add a typed alert_policy to create_server, add WORKBENCH_ALERT_* environment and --alert-* CLI settings that are validated before the socket is bound, report the effective values, their source and a stable sha256 in /api/v1/health and /api/v1/health/history, label a zero policy as debounce_disabled, pass the policy through the deployment boundary, and document the knob without inventing production thresholds.
decision_supported: Which open_after_s and clear_after_s did this specific deployment actually run, can a reviewer verify that from the served evidence and a stable hash, and does a malformed debounce setting stop the process before it can serve monitoring data under a policy nobody approved?
acceptance: create_server accepts a typed alert_policy and a malformed or out-of-bounds policy raises MonitoringPolicyError before BoundedThreadingHTTPServer is constructed, so the process never holds the port while running an unapproved policy

the effective policy is visible in /api/v1/health as monitoring_policy with version backend-monitoring-policy-v1, source, debounce, open_after_s, clear_after_s, history_age_s, max_history and a 64-hex sha256 over exactly those values
the same monitoring_policy block is served by /api/v1/health/history, so the two routes cannot disagree about the policy a single instance runs

a transient single-sample fault cannot open an alert when open_after_s is nonzero, and a transient healthy sample cannot clear an alert when clear_after_s is nonzero, both proven through a real HTTP server reading a real health document
changing a configured value changes both the reported values and the sha256, so a configuration change is visible in the evidence a reviewer cites

the default policy is explicit and documented: DEFAULT_ALERT_OPEN_AFTER_S and DEFAULT_ALERT_CLEAR_AFTER_S are named constants, and a zero/zero policy is reported as debounce_disabled rather than being indistinguishable from an unconfigured instance

the CLI exposes --alert-open-after-s, --alert-clear-after-s, --alert-history-age-s and --alert-max-history, each defaulting to the matching WORKBENCH_ALERT_* variable, following the existing WORKBENCH_* conventions used by the rest of the backend CLI

a malformed debounce setting makes the CLI exit with status 2 and name the offending setting, and an empty or blank value is treated as unset because Compose interpolates an undefined variable to the empty string
the policy source is reported honestly as server-default, environment, command-line or caller, and never claims a source the values did not come from
history bounds in the payload are taken from the effective policy rather than the module-level defaults, so max_history and history_age_s cannot silently disagree with the values the tracker enforces
the deployment boundary passes the WORKBENCH_ALERT_* variables through both compose.yaml and deploy/multi-host/compose.controller.yaml without inventing a default threshold
no production debounce threshold is chosen by this change; the target values remain an Operations/Safety approval and the documented default is the explicit zero policy
no alert-clear, acknowledgement, robot-control, MCU, notification or paging path is added, and the API stays GET-only
the checked-in OpenAPI documents are deliberately not modified: this Packet distinguishes serving the new payload fields from amending the versioned contract, which the Issue's Allowed paths exclude
evidence: pytest output for tests/unit/test_backend_health.py and tests/unit/test_dashboard_accessibility.py with the literal pass count and exit code
ruff check and ruff format --check output over every changed Python file with exit code 0
build/verify.sh output whose final line is OK: no new failures and whose comparison against build/baseline.txt shows no regression
check_task_packet.py --all --base output with exit code 0, proving every Git-visible changed path is inside allowed_paths

test_the_endpoint_reports_the_configured_policy_and_its_change serves both routes over HTTP and asserts the reported source, debounce label, values and differing sha256 for the default versus the configured instance
test_a_transient_single_sample_fault_cannot_open_a_debounced_alert feeds healthy, one faulted and healthy samples through a server with open_after_s=5 and asserts the active alert list is empty

test_a_transient_healthy_sample_cannot_clear_a_debounced_alert opens an alert then feeds one healthy sample inside a 30s clear window and asserts the alert is still active and the status is still fault

test_invalid_policy_values_are_refused_before_anything_listens and test_a_malformed_policy_stops_startup_before_the_socket_is_bound exercise the invalid-policy path, and the latter asserts the CLI exits 2 without calling create_server
test_the_default_policy_is_explicit_and_labelled_disabled and test_the_cli_reports_where_the_policy_came_from pin the documented default and the provenance labels
grep of the startup log target proves service_started.monitoring_policy carries the same block the API serves
make docs builds the MkDocs site with strict mode so the new documentation pages resolve
the full suite comparison in build/verify.sh shows the same pre-existing failures listed in build/baseline.txt, which need a docker CLI or a writable /dev/shm this machine does not have
stop_conditions: Operations/Safety has not approved concrete target debounce windows, so this Packet must not ship any nonzero production default: a nonzero default requires a separate owner-approved change to DEFAULT_ALERT_OPEN_AFTER_S and DEFAULT_ALERT_CLEAR_AFTER_S.
Meeting the acceptance requires editing the checked-in OpenAPI contract, a Pydantic contract in libs/contracts, or an interface schema in interfaces/.
The change would need to clear, acknowledge, deliver or page an alert, or would touch a robot-control or MCU path.
A malformed or out-of-bounds policy can still reach a bound socket, or the effective policy can differ from the one reported in the payload.
A zero policy would be reported without the debounce_disabled label, so an unconfigured deployment could be mistaken for a deliberate one.
The change requires a new configuration framework, a database, a message broker or a writer endpoint.
The change requires editing files owned by another in-flight Issue (#430, #441, #461, #462) in server.py or health.py outside the debounce configuration path.
build/verify.sh is run while another pytest process is active, which would make its repository-wide file snapshot unreliable.
data_classification: internal; tests use synthetic monotonic snapshots, literal non-sensitive environment values and loopback HTTP only, and read no robot, camera or credential data
model_policy: no model call; policy parsing, bounds checking, digesting and payload rendering are deterministic arithmetic and hashing
risks_and_fallbacks: Adding a config knob is new operator surface, and an operator can now set a window that silences a real fault. The owner choice this Packet needs is whether to ship the knob with a zero default or to require an approved nonzero default at the same time.

A nonzero default would change alert behaviour for every existing deployment without an explicit decision. The default therefore stays zero, but it is named, bounded and labelled debounce_disabled instead of being an implicit AlertPolicy().
A very long clear window can hold a cleared-looking fault active for hours. Both windows are bounded to 3600 seconds so the configuration cannot silently outlive the evidence.

Reporting a policy the process does not actually run would be worse than reporting none. The payload is built from the same AlertPolicy object the tracker was constructed with, and the store rebuilds on document reload from that same object.
A blank environment value could be read as zero and silently disable debounce. A blank or whitespace value is normalized to unset, so Compose interpolation cannot change a policy by accident.

An operator could trust the OpenAPI contract for the new fields and find them absent. The contract files are outside this Issue's Allowed paths, so docs/api.md documents the payload and a follow-up Issue must amend the versioned contract; this is recorded as an unmet criterion rather than silently skipped.

Rollback removes the CLI options, the environment pass-through and the monitoring_policy block together, restoring the previous implicit zero policy; a partial rollback that keeps the knob but drops the reporting would make the effective policy invisible again.
